key_insight: Solidification does not always suppress fingering in impacting molten-tin drops; beyond a threshold undercooling it can re-enable fingers by changing rim deceleration and creating mobility contrasts in the spreading liquid.
engineering_relevance: This offers a controllable route to tune splashing and morphology in metal droplet processes, relevant to additive manufacturing and semiconductor debris mitigation.
method: Experiments on impacting molten-tin drops across a range of undercooling levels
Physics-based reduced-order model coupling solidification-modified rim deceleration with mobility-gradient growth
Comparison of estimated solidification time with measured fingering onset and finger-growth termination
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a reversal in the timing between solidification and fingering across temperature, and the reduced-order model reproduces the onset dynamics and final finger length.
watch_item: The mechanism is derived for molten-tin drop impacts, so its transferability to other alloys, substrates, or impact conditions may require re-validation.
paper_title: Re-emergence of fingering in solidifying liquid-metal drops
